Summary of initial forensic review (quick notes):
- The pcap shows multiple upstream requests where the adapter is sending concatenated header frames that the streaming parser on our edge is treating as a single header block. Result: partial header parsing followed by a body frame that the runtime rejects -> stream reset / 502.
- The sdk-wrapper-headers.log shows overlapping writes from the adapter client during high concurrency bursts (we can reproduce with a synthetic driver). The client appears to be sending two HTTP/1.1 chunked frames back-to-back without the expected delimiter when a retry and a proactive prefetch occur concurrently.
- This is client-side framing / header assembly behavior that our parser (which expects canonical chunk delimiters) currently fails to reassemble robustly.

Immediate mitigations to propose:
- Can CheckoutFlow gate the client retry/prefetch concurrently? If so, that will reduce overlap risk while we patch.
- We can deploy a temporary parser-softening rollback that tolerates adjacent header chunks for 48 hours; it increases CPU slightly but buys time.

Attachments: repro-script-smallload.sh (in Drive link)

Laura Bennett
Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p99 latency spikes + 502s on realtime checkout (urgent)

I reproduced locally with the repro driver. Notes:
- Root cause: race in the SDK adapter wrapper where header buffer flush is not synchronized with the retry timer. Under bursty load the wrapper concatenates two header writes; our parser treats that as malformed header block.
- Fix option A (fast): add a short mutex around header writes in the adapter (client). CheckoutFlow can ship a patch in <24 hours; low risk.
- Fix option B (platform short-term): parser-softening on edge to accept concatenated header blocks for N=3 consecutive headers. Lower friction but masked failure modes; requires close monitoring.

Proposed plan:
1) CheckoutFlow devs ship the header-write mutex patch (we’ll provide a minimal patch & test).
2) We deploy parser-softening as a temporary measure during the rollout window and monitor error-rate and CPU.
3) After client patch lands and we validate traffic, remove temporary parser change.

I’ll open a PR for the parser change and tag the incident JIRA.

Marissa Cole
Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime

Team / Elaine —

Short summary (decision record):
- Impact: CheckoutFlow experienced elevated 502s and p99 latency from 07:45 — 11:40 PDT on 2027-07-19. We correlate the root cause to a client SDK race that concatenates header frames under bursty prefetch+retry load.
- Actions taken:
  * 09:30 PDT 7/19: Deployed parser-softening rollback on US-edge for a temporary tolerance window. Decreased 502 rate from ~6% -> ~0.9% within 20 minutes.
  * 10:00 PDT 7/19: Provided CheckoutFlow minimal mutex patch to gate header writes; they validated in staging and started a canary rollout.
  * 11:40 PDT 7/19: Client patch fully deployed for primary fleet; we removed parser-softening at 12:10 PDT after steady state.
- Business outcome: Error-rate returned to baseline; conversion loss estimated <0.6% incremental for the incident window.

Follow-ups (owners & timeline):
- Engineering (Marissa): open a post-mortem and prioritize a parser hardening task (ETA 2 weeks).
- CRM (Laura): follow up with Elaine with a detailed RCA and reproduce steps.
- Sales (Aditya): confirm credit/compensation terms with CheckoutFlow and close deal impact.
